'''Melody A. Swartz''' (born April 1969) is a professor and vice dean for faculty affairs at the [[University of Chicago]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Melody Swartz |url=https://pme.uchicago.edu/faculty/melody-swartz |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=pme.uchicago.edu}}</ref> who pioneered research in engineering complex tissues. Her most cited work "Capturing complex 3D tissue physiology in vitro" has been cited over 1784 times.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Griffith |first1=Linda G. |last2=Swartz |first2=Melody A. |date=March 2006 |title=Capturing complex 3D tissue physiology in vitro |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nrm1858 |journal=Nature Reviews Molecular Cell Biology |volume=7 |issue=3 |pages=211–224 |doi=10.1038/nrm1858 |pmid=16496023 |issn=1471-0080|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Her research is focused on understanding the role of the [[lymphatic system]] regulating immunity in homeostasis and diseases, particularly cancer. She was previously director of the Institute of Bioengineering at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]]. She was elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2023,<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=National Academy of Engineering Elects 106 Members and 18 International Members |url=https://nae.edu/289843/NAENewClass2023 |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=NAE Website}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Dr. Melody A. Swartz |url=https://nae.edu/294314/Dr-Melody-A-Swartz |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=NAE}}</ref> the Royal Academy of Medicine of Belgium in 2023,<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2023-02-07 |title=Melody Swartz elected to the Royal Academy of Medicine of Belgium |url=https://ciic.uchicago.edu/news/melody-swartz-elected-royal-academy-medicine-belgium |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=ciic.uchicago.edu}}</ref> and the [[National Academy of Medicine]] in 2020.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |date=2020-10-19 |title=Melody Swartz elected to the National Academy of Medicine |url=https://pme.uchicago.edu/news/melody-swartz-elected-national-academy-medicine |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=pme.uchicago.edu}}</ref>

== Education ==
Swartz was born in Illinois. She earned her undergraduate degree in [[chemical engineering]] at [[Johns Hopkins University]] (1991) and her PhD in chemical engineering at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (1998). She did her postdoctoral work in the pulmonary division at [[Harvard Medical School]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=The Faculty |url=https://biophysics.uchicago.edu/the-faculty/melody_swartz/ |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=biophysics.uchicago.edu}}</ref>

== Career ==
Swartz began her career working at [[Northwestern University]] in [[Evanston, Illinois]], from 1999 to 2004 as an assistant professor in the chemical, biomedical and bioengineering departments. She served various roles in the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] from 2003 to 2016. first as an assistant professor in the institute of bioengineering, then becoming an associate professor in 2007, finally getting a professorship in 2010 and becoming the institute's director in 2012 until 2014.<ref name=":0" />

In 2014 Swartz took over a part time role in the École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne as she began to transition to working in the [[University of Chicago]]'s Ben May department of Cancer Research and the [[Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering at the University of Chicago|Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering]],<ref name=":0" /> of which she jointly became a professor of both. Swartz is a member of multiple committees at the University of Chicago including the committee on immunology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Faculty and Trainers |url=https://immunology.uchicago.edu/program/faculty |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=immunology.uchicago.edu}}</ref> and the committee on cancer biology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Faculty & Trainers |url=https://cancerbio.uchicago.edu/program/faculty |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=cancerbio.uchicago.edu}}</ref>

Swartz is a member of many college boards and advisory councils. She is a part of MIT's [[Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research|Koch Institute]]'s scientific advisory board<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scientific Advisory Board |url=https://ki.mit.edu/people/scientific-advisory-board |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=ki.mit.edu}}</ref> and has previously served as a strategic scientific advisory board member for the Basel Research Center for Child Health.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof Melody Swartz |url=https://brc.ch/team/melody-swartz/ |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=BRCCH}}</ref>

== Academia ==
Swartz main focus of research throughout her career has been topics relating to cancer, lymphatic immunology and immunotherapy.<ref name=":6" />

Swartz' most cited article "Capturing complex 3D tissue physiology in vitro" was published in March 2006. She talks about creating 3D tissue models in the vitro software. Discussing some design principles for recreating the interwoven set of both biochemical and mechanical cousin the cellular microenvironment and implementing these principles. Emphasizing the involvement of epithelial tissues in 3D models. She mentions two crucial foundations that were crucial for the future of the field. First foundation was the spatial arrangement of cell-surface receptors and the temporal sequence they are presented. The other was a toolbox of biomaterials that should be used for the formation and maintenance of 3D tissues in vitro. This article has been cited 2806 times most recently in 2024 in the article "The potential of graphene coatings as neural interfaces".<ref name=":1" />

=== Editorial positions ===
Swartz is on many journals' editorial boards. She has served on the editorial board of ''Angiogenesis'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Angiogenesis |url=https://link.springer.com/journal/10456/editors |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=SpringerLink}}</ref> a journal covering topics on cellular and molecular mechanisms (2011–present). Swartz is also on the editorial boards of ''[[Cancer Immunology Research]]''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editors |url=https://aacrjournals.org/cancerimmunolres/pages/editors |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=aacrjournals.org}}</ref> (2013–present) and ''[[Biomechanics and Modeling in Mechanobiology]]''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Biomechanics and Modeling in Mechanobiology |url=https://link.springer.com/journal/10237/editors |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=SpringerLink}}</ref> (2015–present).

== Honors ==
*Swartz has received various honors and awards throughout her career.
*On February 7, 2023, Swartz was elected 1 of 106 new members of the [[National Academy of Engineering]]<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> for her work on cancer immunotherapy and vaccination. On that day Swartz was also announced as one of eight international members of the Royal Academy of Medicine of Belgium<ref name=":4" /> for her work in lymphatic vascular biology, immunology and immunotherapy.
*On October 19, 2020 Swartz was announced as a new member of the [[National Academy of Medicine]].<ref name=":5" />
*In 2018 Swartz was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-09 |title=Melody Ann Swartz |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/melody-ann-swartz |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=www.amacad.org}}</ref>
*In 2012 Swartz was made a fellow of the [[MacArthur Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Melody Swartz |url=https://www.macfound.org/fellows/class-of-2012/melody-swartz |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=www.macfound.org}}</ref>
